people.name: Elsie Hanna
people.summary: Elsie arrived in Tauranga in 1922, won the senior championship in 1924 and 1926, and served on the women’s committee from 1926 to 1939. She became the club’s first woman Life Member before 1948.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

people.name: Noel Copestake
people.summary: Noel joined in 1960 and served as captain, president and a member of the inaugural Board. Elected a Life Member in 1997, he contributed to twilight golf, pennant teams and the volunteers known as the Wednesday Firewood Gang.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

people.name: Bernie Child
people.summary: Bernie brought the skills of a machinery contractor to the club’s many volunteer projects. He organised work for the veterans, served as their president in 1995 and built the drinking fountain behind the first tee. His service was recognised with Life Membership in 1997.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

people.name: Hazel Casey
people.summary: Hazel helped beginners, schoolchildren and women new to golf. The supplied feature remembers a Saturday group known as Hazel’s Girls and her support for the introduction of nine-hole golf.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

people.name: Ernie Craig
people.summary: Ernie’s long service helped secure the administration and development of the Racecourse Reserve. Mowat describes his work on the reserve’s management arrangements and his Life Membership of both the golf and racing clubs.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

people.name: Peg Copestake
people.summary: The supplied achievement summary brings together Peg’s playing record, rules knowledge and volunteer service. It records her joining in 1961, her albatross at the sixth hole in 1966, and her work with juniors and new members.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

people.name: H B Lusk
people.summary: Mowat credits H B Lusk with helping design the course when the club moved to the Racecourse Reserve and records Life Membership in 1948–49.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

people.name: A J Mirrielees
people.summary: Mowat describes A J Mirrielees’s work on the extensive planting programme that helped shape the course. He was among the club’s Life Members honoured before 1948.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

people.name: Phyll Sandlant
people.summary: Phyll led the local promotion of women’s nine-hole golf. Her account in Mowat’s book recalls 96 women responding to the first invitation in February 1998, followed by coaching with Rick Barker and support from member volunteers. She became a Life Member in 2006.
people.source: Life Members Landscape.pdf; existing heritage profile supplied 10 November 2026

source_records.title: The 1968 Spalding Masters
source_records.summary: The programme schedules 54 holes on 8–9 January, with a $2,000 purse. Its blank field sheets list entrants; results are supplied separately by the club history.

source_records.title: Preparing Gate Pa: Silvester and Butler
source_records.summary: A contemporary account and photograph of Grant Silvester and Wally Butler preparing the course, including Silvester’s assessment of Commander Harris.

source_records.title: Jim Paterson and the professional shop
source_records.summary: A portrait, professional-shop advertisement and tournament field entry place Jim Paterson within the 1968 club.

source_records.title: Visiting players in the 1968 programme
source_records.summary: Named photographs include Walter Godfrey, Guy Wolstenholme, Martin Roesink, Billy Dunk, Brian Boys, Frank Malloy and other competitors.

source_records.title: Mrs K. Johnston: a national champion
source_records.summary: The programme reports her victory in the preceding August at the New Zealand Māori Ladies’ Championship. Its Johnston spelling differs from Johnstone in the book.

source_records.title: Frank Macklow: golf, cricket and hockey
source_records.summary: A portrait and profile provide sporting and personal context for Macklow’s veterans achievements.

source_records.title: Noel Hockin and the L. C. Smith Rose Bowl
source_records.summary: A profile of regional and club service. The January 1968 programme presents Hockin as still serving, whereas the book gives a 1967 retirement.

source_records.title: Gate Pa’s 1968 scorecard and course views
source_records.summary: The card records 6,025 yards, par 71. An aerial view and photographs from the 18th green show the course and clubhouse.

source_records.title: Honours boards through 1967
source_records.summary: Earlier honours lists complement the book’s appendices. Men’s Open winners for 1966–67 differ between the programme and the book; retain both accounts pending checking.

source_records.title: Early rules reproduced in the programme
source_records.summary: Seventeen rules attributed by the programme to St Andrews in 1812. Their stated provenance is a copy displayed by Harry T. Moore; they are not Tauranga’s tournament rules.

source_records.title: Tauranga in 1968 through its advertising
source_records.summary: Shops, clothing, motels, dining, building trades and transport give the tournament a wider social setting. Inside-cover travel and appliance advertisements and the back cover add further context.

source_records.title: Professionals at the earlier Rotorua Masters
source_records.summary: The named group photograph reproduced in the 1968 programme is from the earlier Rotorua event, not Tauranga’s 1968 field.

corrections.text: Maurice Coad is the correct spelling, not Maurice Code, in two places in Jack Carter’s story.
corrections.status: Applied to the website transcription on 10 November 2026; original DOCX retained unchanged.
